title: al-Kitāb
author: Sībawayh
summary: The first comprehensive grammar of Arabic, treating syntax, morphology and phonology; every later book of naḥw and ṣarf stands on it.

title: al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa
author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
summary: Naḥw arranged as a hundred governors, the words that cause iʿrāb; a first book of grammar in the Indian and Ottoman madrasas, also versified in Persian.

sources.title: ʿAwāmil al-miʾa with Naḥv-i Mīr, Penn Libraries

title: Lāmiyyat al-afʿāl
author: Ibn Mālik
summary: A poem of 114 verses rhyming in lām on the patterns and conjugation of the verb; a ṣarf text of the Maghrib and al-Azhar, with more than ten commentaries.

sources.title: A review on didactic poetry: al-Lāmiyyat al-afʿāl, DergiPark

title: Sharḥ al-Kāfiya
author: Raḍī al-Dīn al-Astarābādhī
summary: The most searching commentary on al-Kāfiya, with a terminology of its own; printed in Istanbul and Lucknow.

sources.title: Sharḥ al-Kāfiya, University of Wisconsin library

title: Sharḥ al-Shāfiya
author: Raḍī al-Dīn al-Astarābādhī
summary: Raḍī al-Dīn's commentary on Ibn al-Ḥājib's handbook of morphology, the fullest classical treatment of ṣarf.

title: Awḍaḥ al-masālik
fullTitle: Awḍaḥ al-masālik ilā Alfiyyat Ibn Mālik
author: Ibn Hishām al-Anṣārī
summary: Ibn Hishām's prose rearrangement and explanation of the Alfiyya, read after Qaṭr al-nadā and Shudhūr al-dhahab.

title: Mughnī al-labīb
author: Ibn Hishām al-Anṣārī
summary: An advanced work on the particles and on how sentences are analysed, written for scholars rather than beginners; commented on by al-Damāmīnī and al-Shumunnī.

sources.title: Al-Munṣif min al-kalām ʿalā Mughnī Ibn Hishām, Durham e-Theses

title: Sharḥ Ibn ʿAqīl
fullTitle: Sharḥ Ibn ʿAqīl ʿalā Alfiyyat Ibn Mālik
author: Ibn ʿAqīl
summary: The plain verse-by-verse commentary on the Alfiyya that most students read with the poem; a standard text of the traditional curriculum.

sources.title: Commentary of Ibn ʿAqīl on the Alfiyya, TAMIU OER
Ibn ʿAqīl's commentary on the Alfiyya, Qatar Digital Library

title: Naḥw-i Mīr
author: al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī
summary: A Persian primer of naḥw in twenty short lessons, the first book of syntax in the Indian and Central Asian madrasas; often printed with al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa.

sources.title: al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī's books, UC Merced (Hurqalya)
Nahv-i Mîr: content and method, OMÜİFD
Nahw Mir: A Primer in Arabic Grammar (English translation), Mecca Books

title: Ṣarf-i Mīr
author: al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī
summary: A Persian summary of Arabic inflection by the same author; part of the ṣarf primers of the Dars-i Niẓāmī with Mīzān al-ṣarf, Munshaʿib and Panj ganj.

title: al-Fawāʾid al-ḍiyāʾiyya
fullTitle: al-Fawāʾid al-ḍiyāʾiyya fī sharḥ al-Kāfiya (Sharḥ Jāmī)
author: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Jāmī
summary: Jāmī's commentary on al-Kāfiya, written for his son; the Kāfiya level of the Indian path and the Molla Câmî of the Ottoman madrasa, with many glosses of its own.

title: al-ʿAwāmil al-jadīda
author: Imām Birgivī
summary: Birgivī's new book of governors: sixty governors, thirty governed words and ten states of iʿrāb, with examples that teach belief and conduct; the Ottoman first book of naḥw.

sources.title: Abdulkahir al-Curcani's al-Avamil and Birgivi's al-Avamil al-Cedid, DergiPark

title: Iẓhār al-asrār
author: Imām Birgivī
summary: Birgivī's second book of naḥw, read after al-ʿAwāmil and before al-Kāfiya in the Ottoman madrasa; especially valued among non-Arab Muslims.

sources.title: Iẓhār al-asrār with al-Kāfiya, Mingana collection (Fihrist)
Imam Birgivi and his place in the Arabic language, İSAM

title: Mutammimat al-Ājurrūmiyya
author: Shams al-Dīn al-Ruʿaynī al-Ḥaṭṭāb
summary: A completion of al-Ājurrūmiyya that keeps its order and adds the rules the short text leaves out; read between al-Ājurrūmiyya and Qaṭr al-nadā.

title: Shadhā al-ʿarf
author: Aḥmad al-Ḥamalāwī
summary: The modern Azhari handbook of ṣarf in three parts (the verb, the noun, and rules for both), printed at Būlāq; the usual ṣarf text after al-ʿIzzī.

sources.title: Shadha al-Urf fi Fan al-Sarf, alkitab.com

title: al-Amthila al-taṣrīfiyya
author: Kiai Maʿṣūm ʿAlī
summary: The ṣarf tables of the Indonesian pesantren, arranged from the bare three-letter verb through the added patterns; read beside al-Ājurrūmiyya.

title: al-Amthila al-mukhtalifa
author: anonymous
summary: The first book of the Ottoman madrasa, learnt by heart: the forms derived from naṣara, first set out mixed by how often they are used (al-Amthila al-mukhtalifa), then each conjugated in full (al-Amthila al-muṭṭarida). The first of the five books of ṣarf, before Bināʾ al-afʿāl, al-Maqṣūd, al-ʿIzzī and Marāḥ al-arwāḥ; its author is unknown, though some commentaries name ʿAlī.

title: Bināʾ al-afʿāl
author: anonymous
summary: The second book of ṣarf in the Ottoman madrasa, read after al-Amthila and before al-Maqṣūd: how the past and present verbs are built, the patterns of the three- and four-letter verb, bare and augmented, with their maṣdars and whether they take an object, ending with the seven kinds of verb. Its author is unknown; it was written in the 6th/12th century or later.

title: al-Maqṣūd
author: anonymous (attributed to Abū Ḥanīfa)
summary: The third book of ṣarf in the Ottoman madrasa: the patterns of the bare and augmented verb and their meanings, the verbal nouns, the weak verbs in brief. Birgivī ascribed it to Abū Ḥanīfa in his commentary Imʿān al-anẓār; no older source confirms it, and its author is otherwise unknown. Rūḥ al-shurūḥ and Birgivī's commentary are read with it.

sources.title: İm'ânü'l-enzâr, a commentary on el-Maksûd, Marmara University

title: Marāḥ al-arwāḥ
author: Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. Masʿūd
summary: The last and fullest of the five books of ṣarf of the Ottoman madrasa, in seven chapters: the sound verb with its augmented and four-letter patterns, then the doubled, hamzated, mithāl, ajwaf, nāqiṣ and lafīf verbs, each conjugated with the changes they undergo. Printed in Istanbul, Būlāq, Delhi and Lahore; commented on by Dikqoz, al-ʿAynī and Ibn Kemal.

title: Mīzān al-ṣarf
author: anonymous
summary: The first book of ṣarf of the Dars-i Niẓāmī, in Persian: the scale faʿala, the kinds of word and of verb, and the conjugation of the bare and augmented verb. Anonymous; printed in the Indian collections of short grammars with Munshaʿib, Panj ganj, Zubdat al-ṣarf and Ṣarf-i Mīr.

sources.title: A collection of short treatises on Arabic grammar (Mīzān al-ṣarf, Munshaʿib, Panj ganj …), University of Wisconsin
Mīzān fī ʿilm al-ṣarf, manuscripts in the British Library (Fihrist)

title: Hidāyat al-naḥw
author: uncertain (ascribed to Sirāj al-Dīn ʿUthmān al-Awadhī, or to Abū Ḥayyān)
summary: The Arabic handbook of naḥw read after Naḥw-i Mīr and before al-Kāfiya in the Dars-i Niẓāmī, in al-Kāfiya's order: a preface, then the noun, the verb and the particle. Its author is uncertain: catalogues name Sirāj al-Dīn ʿUthmān al-Awadhī, others Abū Ḥayyān al-Andalusī. Printed in Kanpur in 1300/1883 with a Persian commentary on the margin.

sources.title: Hidāyat al-naḥw, Princeton manuscript (Digital Scriptorium: on its authorship)
Hidāyat al-naḥw, Kanpur: Nawal Kishor 1300/1883 (Heidelberg University Library)

title: Akhbār al-naḥwiyyīn al-Baṣriyyīn
author: Abū Saʿīd al-Sīrāfī
summary: The reports of the Basran grammarians from Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī to al-Sīrāfī's own teachers: who learnt from whom, what they wrote and the stories told of them. The oldest ṭabaqāt of the grammarians that survives.

sources.title: al-Sīrāfī, Akhbār al-naḥwiyyīn al-Baṣriyyīn (Arabic text, OpenITI)
Sîrâfî, Ebû Saîd, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: Marātib al-naḥwiyyīn
author: Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Lughawī
summary: The grammarians and lexicographers of Basra and Kufa in order of time and rank, with judgements on how far each can be trusted in what he reports of the Arabs; written in Aleppo.

title: Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn
author: Abū Bakr al-Zubaydī
summary: Written in Cordoba for the caliph al-Ḥakam II: the grammarians of Basra in ten generations and of Kufa in six, the lexicographers of both cities, and the scholars of Egypt, Qayrawān and al-Andalus, each entry with teachers, books and reports. The backbone of our generations of the grammarians.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn (Arabic text, OpenITI)
Zübeydî, Ebû Bekir, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ
author: Abū al-Barakāt ibn al-Anbārī
summary: A history of the grammarians and men of letters from Abū al-Aswad, opening with the story of ʿAlī's sheet, to Ibn al-Anbārī's own time, in order of death; short entries, much read.

title: Inbāh al-ruwāt ʿalā anbāh al-nuḥāt
author: Jamāl al-Dīn al-Qifṭī
summary: A large dictionary of the grammarians and lexicographers by the vizier of Aleppo, al-Qifṭī, in alphabetical order, gathering the reports of the earlier ṭabaqāt and of sources now lost.

title: Bughyat al-wuʿāt fī ṭabaqāt al-lughawiyyīn wa-l-nuḥāt
arabic: بُغْيَةُ الوُعَاةِ فِي طَبَقَاتِ اللُّغَوِيِّينَ وَالنُّحَاة
author: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī
summary: The last and largest of the classical ṭabaqāt of the grammarians: more than two thousand grammarians and lexicographers in alphabetical order, down to al-Suyūṭī's own day.

title: Kitāb al-Taṣrīf
author: Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī
summary: The oldest book given wholly to ṣarf that survives: the patterns, the augmented letters, the weak letters and their changes, in the Basran manner of Sībawayh.

title: al-Muqtaḍab
author: al-Mubarrad
summary: A full grammar on Sībawayh's lines by the head of the Basrans in Baghdad, often closer to analogy than al-Kitāb itself; the main book of naḥw between Sībawayh and Ibn al-Sarrāj.

title: al-Uṣūl fī al-naḥw
author: Ibn al-Sarrāj
summary: Sībawayh's grammar set out in a clear order of chapters and divisions, which most later handbooks follow: 'grammar was mad until Ibn al-Sarrāj brought it to reason with his Uṣūl'.

title: Sharḥ Kitāb Sībawayh
author: Abū Saʿīd al-Sīrāfī
summary: The great commentary on Sībawayh's al-Kitāb, many volumes long, explaining its words, its examples and its reasoning; the standard companion of al-Kitāb.

sources.title: Sîrâfî, Ebû Saîd, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: al-Jumal fī al-naḥw
author: al-Zajjājī
summary: A plain handbook of naḥw that became the first book of grammar of al-Andalus and the Maghrib, with more than a hundred commentaries, Ibn ʿUṣfūr's among them.

title: al-Īḍāḥ and al-Takmila
author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
summary: Written for the Buyid ruler ʿAḍud al-Dawla in Shiraz: al-Īḍāḥ on syntax, and al-Takmila on morphology, written, the reports say, when the ruler found al-Īḍāḥ too slight.

sources.title: Ebû Ali el-Fârisî, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: al-Khaṣāʾiṣ
author: Ibn Jinnī
summary: Ibn Jinnī's book on the principles and the inner workings of Arabic: whether language is given or made, evidence and analogy, the causes of grammar, and the 'greater derivation' that finds one meaning in all orders of the same root letters.

title: al-Munṣif
author: Ibn Jinnī
summary: Ibn Jinnī's commentary on al-Māzinī's Kitāb al-Taṣrīf, explaining every rule of ṣarf with its reasons and examples; with its text, the classical treatment of ṣarf before al-Shāfiya.

title: al-Lumaʿ fī al-ʿarabiyya
author: Ibn Jinnī
summary: A short handbook of naḥw in brief chapters, read and commented on for centuries in Iraq, Syria and al-Andalus.

title: Mulḥat al-iʿrāb
author: al-Ḥarīrī
summary: A poem of some three hundred and seventy verses that sets out naḥw for beginners, with its author's own commentary; a school text for centuries before the Alfiyya.

title: al-Mufaṣṣal
author: al-Zamakhsharī
summary: Grammar in four parts, the noun, the verb, the particle and what they share, in short sections; read from Khwārazm to Syria, and the text of Ibn Yaʿīsh's great commentary.

title: al-Inṣāf fī masāʾil al-khilāf
fullTitle: al-Inṣāf fī masāʾil al-khilāf bayn al-naḥwiyyīn al-Baṣriyyīn wa-l-Kūfiyyīn
author: Abū al-Barakāt ibn al-Anbārī
summary: One hundred and twenty-one questions disputed between the Basrans and the Kufans, each with the arguments of both sides and a judgement, usually for Basra: the book through which the debate is known.

title: al-Radd ʿalā al-nuḥāt
author: Ibn Maḍāʾ
summary: The Ẓāhirī judge's critique of the grammarians' method: drop the governor (ʿāmil), the hidden words supplied by taqdīr, the second and third causes, and the exercises in words no Arab said.

title: al-Miṣbāḥ fī al-naḥw
author: al-Muṭarrizī
summary: A short naḥw in five chapters by al-Zamakhsharī's successor in Khwārazm; a reading book in the madrasas of Iran, Central Asia, India and the Ottoman lands, printed with the primers.

title: al-Muqaddima al-Jazūliyya
author: al-Jazūlī
summary: A compressed handbook of naḥw from the Maghrib, also called al-Qānūn, famous for its difficulty and commented on by al-Shalawbīn, Ibn ʿUṣfūr and others.

title: al-Durra al-alfiyya
author: Ibn Muʿṭī
summary: The first grammar in a thousand verses, naḥw and ṣarf together, which Ibn Mālik names at the opening of his own Alfiyya, first to say he surpasses it and then to grant it the merit of coming first.

title: Miftāḥ al-ʿulūm
author: al-Sakkākī
summary: Ṣarf, naḥw and the sciences of meaning and expression in one book; its third part, abridged by al-Qazwīnī, became the rhetoric of the madrasa.

sources.title: Sekkâkî, Ebû Ya'kūb, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: Sharḥ al-Mufaṣṣal
author: Ibn Yaʿīsh
summary: The full commentary on al-Zamakhsharī's al-Mufaṣṣal: for each rule the reasons, the evidence and the views of Basra and Kufa; still the place where students look a question up.

sources.title: İbn Yaîş, Ebü'l-Bekā, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: al-Muqarrab
author: Ibn ʿUṣfūr
summary: The whole of naḥw in clear, numbered divisions by the last great grammarian of al-Andalus.

sources.title: İbn Usfûr el-İşbîlî, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: al-Mumtiʿ fī al-taṣrīf
author: Ibn ʿUṣfūr
summary: One of the fullest books on ṣarf: the patterns, augmentation, and the changes of the weak letters, ibdāl and idghām, case by case.

sources.title: İbn Usfûr el-İşbîlî, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: Tashīl al-fawāʾid
author: Ibn Mālik
summary: Ibn Mālik's prose summa of naḥw and ṣarf, denser than the Alfiyya and fuller; commented on by Abū Ḥayyān, al-Murādī and al-Damāmīnī.

title: Sharḥ Ibn al-Nāẓim
author: Ibn al-Nāẓim
summary: The first great commentary on the Alfiyya, by Ibn Mālik's son, careful and ready to say where the poem is loose; cited by every later commentator.

title: Irtishāf al-ḍarab min lisān al-ʿarab
author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Andalusī
summary: Abū Ḥayyān's summa of naḥw and ṣarf, gathering the views of all the grammarians before him on every question, the Andalusians above all.

sources.title: Ebû Hayyân el-Endelüsî, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: al-Janā al-dānī fī ḥurūf al-maʿānī
author: al-Murādī
summary: The particles of Arabic, from those of one letter to those of five, with their meanings and uses; with Ibn Hishām's Mughnī, the main book on the subject.

sources.title: Murâdî, Hasan b. Kāsım, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: Shudhūr al-dhahab
fullTitle: Shudhūr al-dhahab fī maʿrifat kalām al-ʿarab
author: Ibn Hishām al-Anṣārī
summary: Ibn Hishām's middle handbook, between Qaṭr al-nadā and the Mughnī, with his own commentary; it has much on the iʿrāb of words and the evidence of the Qurʾān.

title: Sharḥ al-Taṣrīf al-ʿIzzī
author: Saʿd al-Dīn al-Taftāzānī
summary: Al-Taftāzānī's first work, by the reports written at sixteen: al-Zanjānī's al-ʿIzzī explained phrase by phrase, read with it in the Ottoman ṣarf course as 'Saʿd al-Dīn'.

title: Sharḥ al-Shāfiya (al-Jārabardī)
author: al-Jārabardī
summary: A plain commentary on Ibn al-Ḥājib's al-Shāfiya from Tabriz; one of the three read with the text and printed in the Majmūʿat al-Shāfiya.

title: Sharḥ al-Shāfiya (al-Niẓām)
author: Niẓām al-Dīn al-Nīsābūrī
summary: A commentary on al-Shāfiya of middle length, known in the madrasas simply as al-Niẓām; a set book of advanced ṣarf in India.

title: al-Maqāṣid al-shāfiya
fullTitle: al-Maqāṣid al-shāfiya fī sharḥ al-Khulāṣa al-kāfiya
author: Abū Isḥāq al-Shāṭibī
summary: A very large commentary on the Alfiyya by the jurist of Granada, verse by verse, with a jurist's care for definitions and evidence.

sources.title: Şâtıbî, İbrâhim b. Mûsâ, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi

title: al-Maqāṣid al-naḥwiyya (al-Shawāhid al-kubrā)
author: Badr al-Dīn al-ʿAynī
summary: Every verse of poetry quoted as evidence in four commentaries on the Alfiyya, with who said it, what it means and where its point lies; printed in the margin of the Alfiyya's commentaries.

title: Malāḥ al-alwāḥ fī sharḥ Marāḥ al-arwāḥ
arabic: مَلَاحُ الأَلْوَاحِ فِي شَرْحِ مَرَاحِ الأَرْوَاح
author: Badr al-Dīn al-ʿAynī
summary: Al-ʿAynī's commentary on Marāḥ al-arwāḥ, the last book of the Ottoman ṣarf course; one of its chief commentaries with Dunqūz's and Kemalpaşazâde's.

title: Sharḥ al-Marāḥ (Dunqūz)
author: Shams al-Dīn Aḥmad, called Dunqūz (Dikgöz)
summary: The commentary on Marāḥ al-arwāḥ most read in the Ottoman madrasas, printed in Istanbul (1306) and Cairo (1309).

title: al-Falāḥ fī sharḥ al-Marāḥ
author: Kemalpaşazâde
summary: The Ottoman şeyhülislâm's commentary on Marāḥ al-arwāḥ, printed in Istanbul in 1289.

title: Hamʿ al-hawāmiʿ
fullTitle: Hamʿ al-hawāmiʿ fī sharḥ Jamʿ al-jawāmiʿ
author: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī
summary: Al-Suyūṭī's own commentary on his Jamʿ al-jawāmiʿ: the views of the grammarians on every question of naḥw and ṣarf in one order, the last great summa of the subject.

title: al-Iqtirāḥ fī uṣūl al-naḥw
author: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī
summary: The principles of grammar, after Ibn Jinnī and Ibn al-Anbārī: what counts as evidence (hearing, consensus, analogy), the causes, and the rules for weighing them.

title: al-Taṣrīḥ bi-maḍmūn al-Tawḍīḥ
author: Khālid al-Azharī
summary: A commentary on Ibn Hishām's Awḍaḥ al-masālik, itself on the Alfiyya; a standard book of al-Azhar.

title: Manhaj al-sālik (Sharḥ al-Ushmūnī)
arabic: مَنْهَجُ السَّالِكِ إِلَى أَلْفِيَّةِ ابْنِ مَالِك
author: al-Ushmūnī
summary: The Azhar's commentary on the Alfiyya: what Ibn al-Nāẓim, al-Murādī and Ibn Hishām had said, gathered into one clear and full text.

title: Ḥāshiyat al-Ṣabbān
author: al-Ṣabbān
summary: The gloss on al-Ushmūnī's commentary, settling its difficulties with the views of the earlier commentators: the last great work on the Alfiyya, still read in Cairo.

title: Ḥāshiyat ʿAbd al-Ghafūr
author: ʿAbd al-Ghafūr al-Lārī
summary: Jāmī's disciple's gloss on al-Fawāʾid al-Ḍiyāʾiyya, read with Sharḥ Jāmī in the Dars-i Niẓāmī and printed in the margin of the Indian lithographs.

title: Ḥāshiyat ʿIṣām
author: ʿIṣām al-Dīn al-Isfarāyīnī
summary: The gloss on Sharḥ Jāmī read after it in the Ottoman naḥw course, known simply as 'İsâm'.

title: Ḥall asrār al-akhyār ʿalā iʿrāb Iẓhār al-asrār
arabic: حَلُّ أَسْرَارِ الأَخْيَارِ عَلَى إِعْرَابِ إِظْهَارِ الأَسْرَار
author: Zeynîzâde Hüseyin Efendi
summary: The iʿrāb of Birgivī's Iẓhār al-asrār word by word, for Ottoman students to check their own analysis; printed many times in Istanbul.

sources.title: Zeynîzâde Hüseyin Efendi, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
